records.name: Friends of Pastorius Park
records.summary: A nonprofit of volunteers who look after the plants, pond and woods of Pastorius Park in Chestnut Hill. They are restoring the park's Northeast Woods, a project that launched with a public event in May 2026.
records.what_you_do: Join seasonal cleanups, tree planting, watering and mulching days, or help with behind-the-scenes tasks.

schedule.text: Volunteer work comes in cleanup and planting seasons. The group posts no fixed weekly schedule. Northeast Woods work runs through fall 2026.

cost.text: No cost to volunteer is listed. Donations are optional.

first_step.how: Sign up through the volunteer page on friendsofpastorius.org for the next seasonal cleanup or planting day
first_step.basis: The group says it always needs new volunteers and has a public sign-up page

records.notes: The group's news page is current (June 2026 post about the May 14, 2026 launch; February 2026 grant news). The group's site gives 8177 Roanoke Street as a physical location; the City list address (200 W Hartwell Ln) is used here, so check which is right before publishing. The City list email (admin@) differs from the site email (info@), and the site email is used. Facebook and Instagram links recorded but not read.

records.name: Friends of Penn Treaty Park
records.summary: A nonprofit that supports Penn Treaty Park on the Delaware River waterfront. It runs a volunteer program, takes donations, and posts park news and a public events calendar.
records.what_you_do: Sign up through the volunteer page to help with park work, donate, or come to events listed on the group's calendar.

schedule.text: The park is open daily from 8 am to 6 pm. Volunteer and event dates were not listed on the pages read.

cost.text: Event and volunteer costs are not listed.

first_step.how: Check the Activities and Events page for the next volunteer day or park event, or email the group at fopenntreatypark@gmail.com to ask how to help

records.notes: The June 2026 news item (a Delaware River Trail closure through September, for construction near the park) has its date taken from the link address, not from the page text, so confidence is medium. The group's site gives 1301 N Beach Street; the City list gives 1299 Beach St, and the City address is used. The City list email (pprstewardship) is not used. The embedded events calendar had no readable events.

records.name: Pennypack Park Trail Advocates
records.summary: A group of mountain bikers who care for the single-track dirt trails in Pennypack Park and work with the city on trail repairs and volunteer trail projects.
records.what_you_do: Help maintain trail sections and join volunteer trail projects that the group coordinates with park staff and other trail groups.

first_step.how: Email Parks and Recreation's stewardship office (pprstewardship@phila.gov) and ask to be connected with this Friends group

records.notes: No website, email or social link found. The summary and the what_you_do text come from a web search summary of trail directory listings (Trailforks and Pinkbike). Both listing pages returned HTTP 403 when fetched, so the facts were not checked on the page and need verifying. The search summary says Parks and Recreation's restoration staff treat this group as their contact for single-track trail issues. The search summary also names Friends of Pennypack Park as a partner, which is listed under leads_only. Kind set to club because the group is not established as a nonprofit; the City list hint is friends_group. Searched once (search budget item).

records.name: Philly Pumptrack
records.summary: A nonprofit bike park on Parkside Avenue with a beginner loop and a larger track with several lines. Volunteers keep the track and bikes in shape, and the group also runs dirt jump sessions and summer camps.
records.what_you_do: Come to a volunteer dig night, usually on Wednesday evenings, to help build and fix the dirt track. Gloves and tools are provided.

schedule.text: Open for the season from about May to late October, weather permitting. Volunteer dig nights are on most Wednesday nights. Hours change on short notice, so check the group's Facebook page first.

locations.label: Philly Pumptrack, next to the Parkside Evans playground

cost.text: No admission fee is listed. Donations are accepted. Visitors sign a waiver.

first_step.how: Come to a Wednesday dig night, sign the waiver on arrival (under 18s need a parent or guardian), and ask how to help
first_step.basis: Dig nights are open to the public, the site lists no experience as required, and the group provides the gloves and tools

records.notes: The City list website (phllypumtrack.org) does not resolve; the group's working address is phillypumptrack.org, used here. Status is dormant because the newest dated item found is from May 2024 (the opening of that season), and the news page has no dated posts. The homepage also says the track is open for the season, but that banner is undated, so the 2026 season may be running; verify before relying on it. The © 2026 footer is not evidence. The Facebook feed showed a login error and was not read. The City list hint is friends_group; kind set to nonprofit because the group describes itself as a 501(c)(3) bike park. No interest tag fits a bike park well, so none is used. Hours change on short notice. Interests set by the orchestrator from the vocabulary synonyms.

records.name: Pleasant Playground Community Garden
records.summary: A community garden on the grounds of Pleasant Playground in East Mt. Airy, started by neighbors who wanted healthy food and a shared green space.
records.what_you_do: Rent a raised bed to grow food. Ask the group or the stewardship office about current plots and work days.

cost.text: Plots were planned at $25 a year, according to 2021 news coverage. The current price is not confirmed.

first_step.how: Email Parks and Recreation's stewardship office (pprstewardship@phila.gov) and ask to be connected with this Friends group

records.notes: The City list gives 305 Slocum St and a website (pleasantplayground19119.org) that now redirects to an unrelated commercial domain. The redirect was not followed, and that link is not used. News coverage places the garden on Chew Avenue: the April 2021 article says the 6700 block and a search summary gives 6757, so 6757 Chew Ave is used. The City list email (pleasantplaygroundgarden@gmail.com) could not be verified and is not published here. The newest dated coverage read is April 2021, so dormant is provisional: a Chestnut Hill Local story on a cleanup (undated in the search summary) returned HTTP 403 and may be newer. Not searched again: the search budget was used. Current state of the garden is unknown.

records.name: Powers Park Conservancy
records.summary: A volunteer group that started in 2013 to keep Powers Park in Port Richmond safe, clean and welcoming. In past years it held spring cleanup days and events for neighbors. Its recent activity could not be confirmed.
records.what_you_do: In past years, volunteers painted benches, planted bulbs and helped with park events. Ask the group or the stewardship office about current work days.

first_step.how: Email Parks and Recreation's stewardship office (pprstewardship@phila.gov) and ask to be connected with this Friends group

records.notes: The newest dated item found is a May 2018 spring service day, listed on the Fairmount Park Conservancy's park site (myphillypark.org). Search summaries of 2017 and 2018 news agree that the group was active then. The page footer shows 2026, which is not evidence, so the group is dormant on current evidence. No closure notice found, so it is not marked defunct. The City list email (powersparkconservancy@gmail.com) could not be verified and is not published here; the orchestrator should decide. The Facebook page was linked but not read. Searched once (search budget item).

records.name: Friends of Pretzel Park
records.summary: A nonprofit that cares for Pretzel Park in Manayunk and runs the park's Saturday farmers market with volunteers. It also hosts drum circles, concerts and kids' story time.
records.what_you_do: Help with park maintenance days, volunteer at the farmers market, or join the email list for news and volunteer calls.

schedule.text: Farmers market on Saturdays, 10 am to 2 pm, rain or shine. Park events such as drum circles and concerts are posted on the site.

cost.text: No admission cost is listed. The group asks for donations.

first_step.how: Visit the Saturday farmers market to meet the volunteers, or sign up for the group's email list at https://lists.friendsofpretzelpark.org/lists/listinfo/PretzelPark to hear about maintenance days
first_step.basis: The market is open to visitors, and the group lists a public sign-up for news and volunteer calls

records.notes: The site lists events through October 2026, and a concerts post dated September 17, 2026. An October 10 drum circle is listed, but its event link says October 8, so that date is unclear. The site lists no email address; sign-up is through the mailing list link. Vendor, performer and park-use forms exist on the site and are not recorded here.

records.name: Friends of Rittenhouse Square
records.summary: A nonprofit that helps look after Rittenhouse Square in Center City. Donors can adopt a bench or sponsor a lawn to help pay for upkeep, and the group runs public events, including a fall craft show and a Halloween family day.
records.what_you_do: Volunteer through the group's volunteer page, become a member, adopt a bench, sponsor a lawn, or come to a public event.

schedule.text: October 2026 events are listed: a fall fine craft show on Oct 9 to 11 (11 am to 5 pm) and Halloween Family Fun on Oct 24 (11 am to 2 pm). The events page gives no location or cost for either.

cost.text: Membership, donation and event costs are not listed.

first_step.how: Go to the Halloween Family Fun on Oct 24 (11 am to 2 pm) or the fall craft show (Oct 9 to 11), or sign up through the volunteer page on the group's website
first_step.basis: Public events are listed with dates, and the group has a public volunteer page

records.notes: The newest news on the homepage is from March 2025; the events page is the current evidence. The events calendar page at /event-calendar/ returned 404, so /events/ is used. The group's office is 201 South 18th Street, Unit 314 (an office, not a meeting place), which is not recorded as a location. The site links a Facebook page by name with no URL, so none is recorded. The kids_ok value is based on the Halloween family event only. The City list address (1800 Walnut St) is used for the square.

records.name: Riverfront North Partnership
records.summary: A nonprofit partnership that promotes the Greenway and riverfront parks in Northeast Philadelphia. It runs cleanup and greening days along the trails and helps local Friends groups, such as the one for Borski Park.
records.what_you_do: Volunteer on cleanup and planting days along the riverfront trails, join the Trailblazer program, or come to free events such as learning to fish at the ponds.

schedule.text: Events are posted as they come up rather than on a set weekly schedule. Learn to Fish is first come, first served at the ponds; its date is not shown on the page.

cost.text: Learn to Fish is free. Costs for other programs are not listed.

first_step.how: Sign up through the volunteer page at riverfrontnorth.org/get-involved-donate/volunteer/ and watch for the next cleanup or the free Learn to Fish day
first_step.basis: Volunteer sign-up and events are public, and the group explains how to get involved on its site

records.notes: The City list calls this group Friends of Riverfront North (alias Lardners Point Park). The group calls itself Riverfront North Partnership (RNP), so that name is used. The July 2026 news item (a bike parade at Borski Park on July 1) gives the last sign of life. The City list email (brian@) is an individual's address and is not published; the group's own info address is used. The office is at 3460 N Delaware Ave, Suite 306, Philadelphia 19134. The City address for Lardner's Point Park is used as the location. The Friends of Borski Park is a sub-group that is listed under leads_only.

notes: Budget: 3 of 3 WebSearch calls used (Pennypack Park Trail Advocates, Powers Park Conservancy, Pleasant Playground). 21 of 60 WebFetch calls used. Six groups had no website and were not searched because the budget ran out: Friends of Paolone Park, Friends of Pop's Park, Friends of Poquessing Watershed, Rainbow De Colores Friends Group, Friends of Ralph Brooks, Friends of Ridgway Park. They are written as status unknown with low confidence and are the first job for the next wave. Verdicts: 15 publish, 0 hide, 0 other. Status counts: 5 active (Pastorius, Penn Treaty, Pretzel, Rittenhouse, Riverfront North), 3 dormant (Philly Pumptrack, Pleasant Playground, Powers), 7 unknown. Facebook pages were linked but never read (platform rule). City list problems: the Philly Pumptrack domain is misspelled on the City list (phllypumtrack.org does not resolve; phillypumptrack.org works and is used); the Pleasant Playground website on the City list redirects to an unrelated commercial domain, which was not followed. City list emails were not published when they could not be verified (Pop's, Pleasant Playground, Powers, Paolone none); the orchestrator should decide.
